claim: When a supplier listing folds rows past a top-N by volume, lift every row carrying the attribute the surface exists for (a politician tie) and let the fold sentence assert that no folded row carries it, because a volume cut silently hides exactly the rows the reader came for.
because: Brno's trail folded 4 of its 13 MP-tied counterparties (ranks 13-16) into 'a dalsich 5 protistran' with no word; measured against the store, fixed in politicas 2303040 with a pure liftTiedRows split under test.

claim: When adding an identity tiebreak to a comparator, first check whether the previous stable sort was carrying an order the caller relied on (input pre-sorted by a field), because appending id right after the primary key replaces that implicit order with id order and the doc comment keeps promising the old one.
because: politicas 26d695a (a correct repo-wide total-order fix) turned the town picker's within-tier population order into ICO order; 'pra' returned a 572-person village ahead of an 11 119-person town. Fixed in 22f03d6 by naming the population term explicitly; the test now feeds the input reversed.

claim: When a comparison prints one period over both the subject and its peer benchmark, compute the benchmark at the subject's period (and size the bars from that period too), because a benchmark taken at the dataset's latest period is only correct while every subject reports it.
because: politicas /rozpocty printed the town's last reported year over both bars while the median was always the batch's last year; equal today only because 132/132 towns report 2025. Fixed in 785faf0 by passing the year index; tested synthetically.

claim: When a money trail sums per-counterparty rows, name the total after the join grain (contract relationships, contract x counterparty), not contracts, because a contract with two graph firms lands in two rows and the batch carries no id to de-duplicate on.
because: politicas: 11 741 row-counts vs 11 582 municipal contracts (+1,4 %); relabelled in 2d11dae with the measurement in the field's doc comment.

claim: When a deterministic language gate adds a morphology (word-shape) rule beside its closed stopword lists, count shape hits only as corroboration of a closed-list hit and let them decide alone only above a density floor, because the other language's ordinary word forms (Czech -ly plural past tense, -hled nouns) match English shapes and one hit then withholds correct prose.
because: politicas pass-74 corpus, 1 966 reader-facing strings: morphology deciding alone withheld 4 Czech reviewer notes; a floor of 3 kept the single English note withheld and freed all 4 (13 -> 9), catalog 13 -> 11

claim: When a server/client bundle boundary is guarded by a lint rule that tolerates `import type` from server modules, give the rule a strict mode that forbids even type imports once every server module's types have a pure sibling home, because a type-only import still couples the client file to the server module and the next value specifier added to that line is a bundle breach that reviews as 'a type moved'.
because: politicas 0b217ff: 29 client type-imports across 9 loaders moved to sibling *Types.ts, then the rule's typeImports:"forbid" measured 0 violations and turned the ADR's prose acceptance criterion into an enforced one; default kept 'allow' so the package's external preset contract did not change.

claim: When a data layer pairs a bound-column array with a row mapper per table, add one parity test that asserts the mapper's output keys equal the camel-case of the array, because a column bound on write but never read (or read but never bound) coerces silently to a default and no runtime signal ever fires.
because: politicas 1c035c4: ten table pairs in lib/db/pglite/mappers.ts had drifted by nothing yet and had no guard; the parity test is 12 lines per table and turned the implicit contract into a failing test.
